newsitem.title: USA: Vivus says shipment reduction due to FDA.
newsitem.headline: Vivus says shipment reduction due to FDA.

text.p: Vivus Inc said Monday it would temporarily reduce shipments of MUSE (alprostadil) to customers, estimated to extend from March 20 to April 10, 1997.

The company said the reduced shipments resulted from a diversion of efforts of laboratory personnel during the first post-approval FDA inspection of the Vivus manufacturing facility. During this inspection, certain deficiencies were noted. The company said it is resolving these deficiencies as outlined in a March 24 response to the FDA. During this period, the production of MUSE (alprostadil) continued at full capacity.

"Although our plant has been producing and continues to produce at its current capacity, the release of product has temporarily slowed. This has had the effect of reducing product availability during this period,"said David Yntema, Vivus' chief financial officer.

"We regret the slowdown in delivery of product to our wholesalers, pharmacies, physicians and patients, but we expect to resume normal product delivery rates by mid-April in addition to clearing all manufactured but unreleased product by the end of April," he said.
